name: Fish and Wildlife Biology PhD
detailsNote: Official information available; Fall 2027 dates not confirmed.
summary: Research doctorate in fish and wildlife ecology requiring agreement from a faculty major professor.

publishedDeadlines.label: Application materials
publishedDeadlines.note: A faculty member recruiting for a research-assistantship-funded position may communicate a different date. No entry year stated.

applicationFee.note: First application $70; further applications within 12 months $25. No need-based waivers. Documented McNair Scholars and UM undergraduate TRIO students have category waivers; advertised program waivers must be requested from program. Confirm applicable international category eligibility.

english.note: TOEFL Essentials 9 or MET 58 also listed. A degree taught primarily in English can exempt testing with language-of-instruction verification; listed-country exemptions also apply. Provisional options exist but must be determined by department/Graduate School.

documents: Three responses, each capped at 300 words: degree motivations/goals; proud accomplishment; capacity to learn/adapt/challenge oneself/complete a project
requirements.note: GPA minimum 3.0 undergraduate and 3.5 graduate. Most entrants have a master’s, but strong bachelor’s applicants considered. Usually wildlife biology or related preparation; alternative backgrounds depend on ecological expertise and advisor. No admission without major-professor agreement.

funding.note: Program usually admits only when funding is available, with rare exceptions; aid review separate, no special form. TA/RA opportunities depend on funding. Central international guidance warns many programs do not offer first-year teaching appointments to students from non-English-speaking countries; some offer international research appointments. Confirm individual offer; no universal guarantee.
